title: Treasury, 2023, 2023 Intergenerational Report: Australia's future to 2063
what_taken: Population 26.5 million in 2022-23 to 40.5 million in 2062-63; growth 1.1% a year over 40 years against 1.4% over the past 40 (p. 39, p. 37); net overseas migration fixed at 235,000 (p. 38); projections do not account for climate change (p. 227); higher case +3.1 million (p. 254).
notes: Government framing of the population debate. Page numbers are printed numbers. Current official PDF on the Treasury site.

title: Treasury, 2021, 2021 Intergenerational Report
what_taken: Population projected to reach 38.8 million in 2060-61, the first downward revision in an intergenerational report, from the pandemic and lower fertility (p. 14, also p. viii); population in June 2050 of 35.3 million against 37.8 million in the 2015 report (Table A2.1.1, p. 158); net overseas migration 235,000.
notes: Earlier edition kept for the change between reports. Printed page numbers.

title: Centre for Population, 2025, 2025 Population Statement
what_taken: Population 27.5 million in March quarter 2025; 28 million by end of 2025-26 and 41 million by 2065-66 (Table 1, p. 1); long-run net overseas migration 235,000, fertility 1.42 in 2025-26 rising to 1.62 (p. 1); case study holding population at 30 million needs net overseas migration of 32,000 a year by 2035-36 (Box 1, p. 4).
notes: Latest statement listed on the Centre site on 2026-11-11 (data files dated 2026-01, PDF file folder 2026-03). Printed page numbers.

title: Productivity Commission, 2023, Review of Part 3 of the Future Drought Fund Act, Inquiry report no. 102 (8 September 2023)
what_taken: Fund makes $100 million a year available for drought resilience (p. v); fund is establishing a solid foundation but needs a stronger focus on lasting public benefits (Key points, p. 2); drought now treated as a business risk, with policy shifted to self-reliance and preparedness (p. 3); $400 million allocated under the first Funding Plan (p. 6).
notes: Version posted on the Commission site (file folder dated 2025-10, report dated 8 September 2023). Page numbers are printed numbers; the $400 million page is read from PDF page 16 and its printed number was not checked.
